reason.stale-token: Its sign-in has expired. Sign in again.
reason.version-below-range: It works, but {{version}} is older than the versions Agentry has been tested with ({{range}}).
reason.version-above-range: {{version}} is newer than what Agentry knows how to use ({{range}}). Install an earlier one and choose it here.
reason.version-unreadable: Its version could not be read, so Agentry cannot tell whether it is compatible.
reason.probe-timeout: It could not be checked: it did not answer in time.
reason.spawn-denied: This system does not let Agentry run the program. Check its permissions.
reason.spawn-failed: The program was found but would not start.
reason.binary-not-found: There is no trace of {{label}} on this machine.
reason.config-home-only: There is configuration in {{home}}, but the program cannot be found.
reason.missing-required-command: A command it needs is missing on this machine.
reason.unsupported-platform: It does not run on this operating system.
reason.handshake-failed: It started but did not answer the way Agentry expects.
reason.capability-missing: It is missing something Agentry needs from it in this version.
reason.no-probe: Agentry cannot check this one yet.
reason.auth-required: It needs a sign-in the vendor's own tool has to ask for.
reason.schema-untested: Its structured output was not tested on this version, so Agentry does not use it for that.
reason.busy: It is busy with another session and could not be checked now.
reason.disabled: It is not searched for or checked while it is off.
reason.limit-reached: It reached its usage limit and has not reset yet.
reason.limit-near: It is close to its usage limit.

row.checking: Reading the version and the sign-in…

firstRun.label: First start
firstRun.title: These are the agents on your machine
firstRun.checkingTitle: Looking for agents on your machine
firstRun.intro: Agentry looked in your terminal's PATH and the usual install folders. You start with the first one that is ready; the order and the rest you change later in Settings.
firstRun.introPhone: You start with the first one that is ready. The order and the rest you change later in Settings.
firstRun.watching: Agentry keeps watching your folders: what you install or sign in to in a terminal shows up here by itself.

empty.title: No agent found
empty.body: Agentry looked in your terminal's PATH and the usual install folders, and there is none. Install one and it will show up here by itself.
empty.install: See how to install Claude Code

intro: The coding agents Agentry finds on this machine. If you install one or sign in from a terminal, this list updates on its own.

default.title: Default provider
default.hint: New chats use it. With “Automatic” it is the first one that is ready, in the order of this list: drag the handle to change the order.
default.hintPhone: New chats use it. Move a provider up or down to change the order.
default.autoHint: The first ready, in this order

order.handle: Move {{name}}. Use the up and down arrows to change its place.

bin.title: {{name}} binary
bin.hint: Agentry uses this program instead of searching the PATH. Before saving it, it reads its version and checks it is inside the tested range ({{range}}).
bin.hintNoRange: Agentry uses this program instead of searching the PATH. Before saving it, it reads its version and checks it works.
bin.cleared: {{name}} now uses the one on PATH

limit.title: Limit
limit.unknown: The last reading is out of date, so the limit is not known until a new one arrives.

onLimit.title: When a provider reaches its limit
onLimit.intro: What Agentry does with the work it launches itself (flows, the tasks of an orchestration, the assistant) when its provider reaches the usage limit. Nothing in your own chat moves by itself: it asks you, and the action here comes first.
onLimit.default: Waiting for the reset is what a fresh install does. It sends no work and no summary to another provider until you turn that on here.

action.label: What to do
action.aria: What to do at a limit

handoff.label: Continue with a handoff
handoff.hint: Carries on in the next ready provider, in the same worktree, with a summary of what was asked, what was done and what is left.

restart.label: Start over
restart.hint: Starts again in the next ready provider, in the same worktree, from the original prompt.

wait.label: Wait for the reset
wait.hint: Resumes in the same provider when its limit resets. Spends nothing on another.

allowed.label: What a decision may choose
allowed.hint: Only counts when the “What to do at a limit” point in Decisions is in Shadow or Active. It never chooses outside this.

maxWait.label: Longest wait
maxWait.hint: When Agentry does not know when the limit resets, it waits this long and then fails the work. From {{min}} to {{max}} h.
maxWait.short: No reset date: it waits this long, then fails. 1 to 48 h.

maxMoves.label: Provider changes per piece of work
maxMoves.aria: Provider changes per piece of work
maxMoves.hint: Past this number the work waits instead of hopping between providers. From {{min}} to {{max}}.

map.title: Model mapping
map.intro: When work moves from one provider to another, it uses the counterpart model you choose here. With no counterpart the work waits for the reset and tells you. Nothing enters on its own: a suggestion does not count until you accept it.
map.needTwo: The mapping needs two providers that are on and list their models.
map.waitingTitle: A job is waiting for this counterpart.
map.waitingBody: {{model}} has no counterpart on one of the providers. Choose one and the job carries on when the limit resets.
map.notInForce: It does not count until you accept it.
map.suggestNone: Nothing to suggest for this model right now
map.suggestFailed: Could not ask for a suggestion
map.noneHint: No model here can stand in for it: the work waits
map.staleHint: {{provider}} no longer lists this model: it is treated as if there were no counterpart.
map.waitsHere: Work with this model waits for the reset.

retire.title: Agentry no longer switches Claude accounts
retire.lead: Work now moves from one provider to another when one reaches its limit. This notice appears once.

account.label: Account in use
account.body: , the one claude-swap left active. Claude Code uses it as before. To change it, sign in to Claude Code again or save a token in

changed.label: What changed
changed.body: When a provider reaches its limit, work no longer rotates accounts: it continues on another provider with a handoff, starts over there or waits for the reset. You choose in “When a provider reaches its limit”. Until you change it, it waits.

policies.label: Policies removed
policies.body_one: {{count}} project had a rotation policy that no longer exists. Open its provider order:
policies.body_other: {{count}} projects had a rotation policy that no longer exists. Each opens its provider order:

left.label: Left alone
left.body: claude-swap and its accounts are where they were, and cswap still works from a terminal.

retire.removeBody: This deletes only the copy Agentry installed in its data folder. claude-swap's own accounts and files are not touched.
retire.removeHint: Deletes only the one Agentry installed in its data folder. Nothing else.
retire.removed: Agentry's copy of claude-swap was removed
retire.nothingToRemove: There was no copy to remove

home.keeps: Claude Code keeps using {{account}} · work moves between providers
home.keepsNone: Claude Code keeps its account · work moves between providers

project.title: Providers
project.intro: Which agents this project may use and what its work does at a limit. Each setting inherits the global one until you change it.
project.outsideHint: A provider outside the order never gets this project's work.
project.actionAria: What to do at a limit in this project
